title: Extension bundles install without signature verification
description:
ExtensionInstaller.swift:46-64 installs any .crx/.xpi/.zip by stripping the CRX header (ExtensionArchive.swift:67) and writing the ZIP to disk; the CRX2/CRX3 signature is never validated and unsigned .xpi/.zip install with no provenance. Anyone who opens a malicious bundle runs its code with full extension privileges. WebKit provides no signing store, so the browser must check.

DECISION (2026-08-07): trust model is WARN-BUT-INSTALL. Unknown or missing signer is not blocked; the UI shows an unverified-developer warning before the bundle is enabled. Verified signatures from a pinned key are trusted silently. No paid Apple signing identity required.
design: Verify CRX2/CRX3 signatures against a pinned public key (store key or developer key); unknown/missing signer is allowed but flagged in the UI before enable. .xpi/.zip carry no signature, so they always take the warn path. Reuse ExtensionArchive byte parsing; keep bundle load path unchanged. Surface verification result (verified / unverified) on the extension row and in an install-time confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: CRX2/CRX3 signatures are actually verified against a pinned public key (not stripped-and-ignored); unsigned .xpi/.zip and unknown-signer bundles still install but the UI shows an unverified-developer warning at install and on the extension row, and they are not silently trusted; tampered bundles are detected and flagged; tests cover tampered, unsigned, valid, and unknown-signer bundles
close_reason: CRX2/CRX3 signatures verified at install in new ChordCrypto package; warn-but-install UI (row icon, install message, enable confirmation); verdict persisted as <slug>.verification; 10 verifier + 4 installer + 3 UI tests; prepush green

title: YouTube page freezes after ad (no scroll, no click)
description:
User report: after an ad is skipped/fast-forwarded on first load, the whole watch page becomes non-interactable once the ad ends — no scroll, no click — until the tab is closed.

Root cause: skipping/rate-blasting an ad triggers YouTube's anti-adblock enforcement wall. YouTubeAdBlocker's CSS only hides the wall's dialog (tp-yt-paper-dialog:has(ytd-enforcement-message-view-model)); the wall is a modal iron-overlay whose open handler pins a full-screen tp-yt-iron-overlay-backdrop (swallows all pointer events) and sets body overflow:hidden (locks scroll). The overlay's close path never runs for a CSS-hidden element, so the page stays frozen after the ad.

Fix (YouTubeAdBlocker.swift): a MutationObserver dismantles the wall — removes ytd-enforcement-message-view-model (climbing to its TP-YT-PAPER-DIALOG host so the overlay stack isn't left with an orphan), removes a visible tp-yt-iron-overlay-backdrop, restores documentElement/body overflow, and best-effort resumes the paused player. Kept the CSS hide as fallback. Added test anchor YouTubeAdBlockerTests.dismantlesEnforcementWall. Verified: swift build -warnings-as-errors clean, full suite 602 tests green.
close_reason: Fixed: YouTubeAdBlocker now dismantles the enforcement wall (removes the iron-overlay backdrop + restores overflow) via MutationObserver instead of only CSS-hiding the dialog. Build clean, 602 tests green.

comments.author: Doddy Rizal Novianto
comments.text: Verified manually (2026-08-14): with the fix in place, skipping/fast-forwarding the pre-roll ad no longer freezes the page — scroll and clicks work after the ad ends. No regression in ad skipping or mute behavior.

title: Fix: YouTube fullscreen video renders black until app is relaunched
description:
User report: sometimes the YouTube player goes fully black in video fullscreen (YouTube's own fullscreen button). Exiting fullscreen (Esc/F) restores the normal page, but re-entering fullscreen is black again, and only quitting Chord fixes it. Reloading the tab does not help.

Root cause: macOS WebKit element-fullscreen reparenting bug (webkit.org/b/313802, reproduced on macOS 26). When a page element goes fullscreen, WKWebView is replaced by a placeholder, moved into a WebKit-owned fullscreen window, then moved back (WKWebView.fullscreenState docs). If the web view is AutoLayout-governed from an ancestor (SwiftUI hosting view), it comes back at a collapsed 0x0 frame and fullscreen video renders black persistently.

Fix (uncommitted, local):
- WebSurfaceContainerView.install: WKWebView now uses frame + autoresizing [.width,.height] instead of Auto Layout constraints (the documented workaround).
- LiveWebView observes WKWebView.fullscreenState; on .notInFullscreen it re-anchors the web view frame to the container bounds and forces a repaint, and logs every transition to the AppLog.

Verification: prepush green (601 tests). Needs a real-app pass: enter/exit YouTube fullscreen repeatedly, especially after the sidebar/pane is resized.
close_reason: User verified manually: black YouTube fullscreen no longer reproduces (2026-08-11). Fix shipped; see ADR 019.

title: Content-blocker weekly refresh is all-or-nothing across both lists
description: ContentBlocker.swift:104-112 concatenates EasyList + EasyPrivacy into one combined string; if either fetch fails the entire refresh aborts and defers to next launch (lastRefresh untouched), so one flaky URL costs both lists for a week. Also hashes/compiles them as one unit, so a change in one list invalidates the other's compiled chunks.
design: Fetch, hash, compile, and store each list under its own identifier (per-list shortHash); track lastRefresh per list; keep the seed fallback and the existing content-hash cache-hit behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A failure fetching EasyList does not lose an already-fetched EasyPrivacy update and vice versa; each list refreshes independently; compiled chunks are keyed per list so a change to one does not invalidate the other's cache
close_reason: ContentBlocker refreshes each list independently (per-list hash identifiers, per-list lastRefresh keys, failed list keeps last good set and retries); seed fallback for never-refreshed slots; legacy single-key migrated read-once; 11 engine tests incl. 3 new per-list; prepush green

title: User-Agent version tokens are stale and internally inconsistent
description: WebKitEngine.swift:370 hard-codes 'Version/26.5 Safari/605.1.15' as the live UA suffix, while UserAgent.swift:34 prefills the Settings custom field with Version/17.5 (defaultTemplate) and the presets carry 17.5/126/127 too. The app advertises two different Safari versions, and the token is hard-coded so it drifts from the actual WebKit engine version over time. UA-vs-engine feature mismatch is itself a fingerprint signal.
design: Centralize the Safari version token in one constant (e.g. in ChordCore next to UserAgent.swift) and have WebKitEngine.swift:370 + UserAgent.swift:34 reference it. Match the token to the SDK's shipped WebKit version.
acceptance_criteria: Live UA suffix and the Settings prefill/template come from one source of truth and cannot drift; version matches the shipped WebKit/Safari token; existing unit tests for UserAgentRules and UA application still pass
close_reason: UserAgentPreference.safariVersionToken is the single source of truth; defaultTemplate builds from it and WebKitEngine.safariUserAgentSuffix references it; new ChordCore + ChordEngine tests pin the invariants; prepush green

title: YouTube ad sometimes not skipped or fast-forwarded
description: YouTubeAdBlocker tick() fails intermittently: an ad plays to the end instead of being skipped/fast-forwarded. Suspected causes in Packages/Sources/ChordEngine/YouTubeAdBlocker.swift: (1) once-only playbackRate bump that YouTube's player resets to 1x, (2) skip-button click returns early and swallows the fallback seek/blast when the button is disabled/custom, (3) targets only the first <video> while YouTube A/B-tests ads on a separate element and the watch page has an ambient background video.
close_reason: Re-assert playbackRate every tick (YouTube resets it to 1x, so the once-only bump died), removed the early-return after skip-click so the seek/blast fallback always runs, blast every <video> instead of the first, and seek-to-end only when duration is ad-length (<=60s) so stitched ads can't skip the content.
